approval.decision: Owner instruction in this session on 2026-11-26, answering the session's request to approve echelon-current 1.43.0. The owner had asked on 2026-11-25 to "Release what you need to adopt the echelon theme and do any house cleaning you need to do"; the session released Praxis 3.26.0 (Praxis web and hub pages on Forma 1.0.1 with the Echelon theme 1.1.0) and Arca 0.7.1 (packages rebuilt against Aegis 2.0.2 instead of 1.0.0, public API unchanged), proposed this set, and said it would ask for approval once REG-RU-007 passed. The owner answered "I approve". The exact minute is approximate: the answer arrived shortly after 00:11Z. The set selects exactly that move: Praxis 3.25.0 -> 3.26.0 and Arca 0.7.0 -> 0.7.1, nothing else

Replaced by Forma 1.0.1 (v1.0.1, 0ddbfc96), the 1.0 major release line (forma#182) with the codemod fixes of forma#183. Breaking for every consumer: Forma is brand-neutral (BNR-001, EDS-ADR-002) and its ef- namespace is renamed forma- (FORMA-NS-001: every .ef-* class, --ef-* property, data-ef-* attribute and <ef-*> tag; data-ef-brand is data-forma-brand); dist/brands/echelon.css (export ./brands/echelon.css) and the Echelon marketing bundles forma-echelon-marketing.css and forma-marketing-theme-echelon.css are removed, and the Echelon brand is the optional echelon-theme 1.0.0 selected beside it. Applications migrate with the shipped F# codemod tools/NamespaceMigrator and, if Echelon applications, add echelon-theme; an application that has not migrated stays on 1.37.2. The profile's Forma range moves to >=1.0.0 <2.0.0 for this. License PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0 (read from the published package.json). Every asset digest re-hashed from download matches GitHub's API digest; forma-all.css and forma-marketing.css match forma-marketing.sha256

Replaced by Arca 0.7.1 (v0.7.1, 0004c7d4; WI-0044, arca#52), a patch release: source and public API unchanged from 0.7.0; the packages are rebuilt so that EchelonFoundry.Arca.GitHub and EchelonFoundry.Arca.Limen depend on EchelonFoundry.Aegis.Core and EchelonFoundry.Aegis.Integration.GitHub 2.0.2 (0.7.0: 1.0.0), so a consumer on echelon-current no longer restores Aegis 1.0.0 through Arca beside the selected Aegis 2.0.2. Arca.Core has no Aegis dependency; the FSharp.Core floor stays 10.1.400 and Arca.Limen still needs EchelonFoundry.Limen.Store and .Contract 0.9.0 (limen-fsharp 0.9.0 selected). Consumer note: CallFailure.Failed and ServerError carry Aegis's GitHubFailure.T from the Aegis 2 assembly, so an application that references Aegis directly must be on 2.0.2 or later (selected since 1.42.0). License PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0 in all three nuspecs (read from the downloaded packages). The three .nupkg files re-hashed from download match checksums.txt and GitHub's API digests, and each verifies with gh attestation verify (release.yml on main at 0004c7d4). Conditor has no Arca descriptor: released Conditor accepts it as an unlisted nuget-library (REG-RU-007). Chrona's arca 0.5.0 incompatibility is unchanged (see 0.5.0)

Replaced by Aegis 2.0.2 (NuGet EchelonFoundry.Aegis.Core 2.0.2 from 711e0260, aegis#26), a patch: in 2.0.0 and 2.0.1 capture and captureReported waited synchronously (Async.RunSynchronously) for the fault record even with the default Detached persistence, so a single-threaded WebAssembly host froze on its first fault (found by Summa's browser fault test; Signal and Vigila carry the same latent hang). 2.0.2 starts a detached record and returns without any blocking wait; Blocking still awaits. No public signature changes and the FSharp.Core floor stays 10.1.400 (all three 2.0.2 nuspecs read from the nuget.org downloads). The package digest was re-hashed from the nuget.org download. 2.0.1 stays registered for the approved 1.41.0 set, which is not changed
